name: Henrika Domnathi // Henrika, Infernal Seer
oracle_text:
Flying
At the beginning of combat on your turn, choose one that hasn't been chosen —
• Each player sacrifices a creature of their choice.
• You draw a card and you lose 1 life.
• Transform Henrika.
blocked_sentences: At the beginning of combat on your turn, choose one that hasn't been chosen —

needs.what: A modal ability whose already-taken modes are struck off the list on later resolutions: `choose_mode` needs to record, per source permanent, which mode indices that ability has already run, and offer only the rest -- with the whole ability doing nothing once every mode is spent. Roughly a `once_each: true` (or `exclude_chosen`) flag on `choose_mode` plus a per-object ledger of used indices, keyed by ability so two modal abilities on one permanent do not share a tally.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `op_choose_mode` (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_control.py) builds its labels straight from `spec['modes']` every time it resolves and calls `ask_mode` with the full list; a mode is a `{label, effects}` pair and the loader's per-mode validation (`_validate_effect`, src/automtg/cards/loader.py) accepts no availability condition, so there is no place to hang "only if not yet chosen". Nothing in the engine tracks mode usage -- there is no `chosen_modes`/`modes_used` field on a game object, and `Game._ask_modes` likewise passes the printed list through untouched. The nearest tool, `set_flag`/`has_flag`, only writes a word on the permanent and reads it back inside an `if`: guarding each mode's body with `{"not": {"has_flag": "henrika_mode_1"}}` still OFFERS the used mode, so a player could pick a spent mode and have the trigger resolve for nothing, which is not the printed choice. The alternative approximation -- leaving the modes unguarded -- is strictly a different, much stronger card: a Henrika that can transform every combat, or drain every combat. Both are refused as approximations.

notes: The two-faced authoring half of this card is SOLVED and must not be re-opened. An answer file may now carry a `back` key beside `card`, the front face names it with `back_face`, `link_faces` refuses a one-way link, and `tests/cards/test_authoring.py::TestATransformingCardIsOneAnswer` witnesses it. The engine side (GameState.card_of, CardDef.back_face, the `transform` op, the shipped bloodline_keeper / lord_of_lineage pair in data/cards/edgar.cards.json) was never missing.

Every other printed line is already expressible: `flying` is a keyword; `begin_combat` is a trigger event; "Each player sacrifices a creature of their choice" is the `for_each_player` + `sacrifice` idiom already shipped on Zurgo's "each opponent sacrifices a creature of their choice"; "You draw a card and you lose 1 life" is `draw` + `lose_life`; "Transform Henrika" is the `transform` op. Only the modal exclusion clause blocks the card.

The packet carries only the front face's own lines (flying and the modal trigger) plus the joined type line, so the back face's printed text is not in hand here; whatever it turns out to be, nothing blocks writing it, because the front face is what cannot be said. When `modes-not-yet-chosen` lands, this card should be re-queued as a single two-faced answer, not re-triaged as an authoring-pipeline problem.
